dedupe_keys.name: canada s core public infrastructure survey ccpi

description: Canada's Core Public Infrastructure Survey (CCPI) is a mandatory Statistics Canada survey, designed with Infrastructure Canada, of the inventory, condition, performance and asset management of core public infrastructure owned or leased by Canadian governments. The 2022 cycle covers twelve asset classes, among them potable water, wastewater and stormwater assets, roads, bridges and tunnels, public transit, solid waste, social housing, active transportation and natural infrastructure. Municipalities of at least 1,000 residents are surveyed as a census and smaller ones sampled, together with regional, provincial, territorial and federal owners and Crown corporations; estimates are weighted and imputed, and published nationally, by province and territory, and by urban or rural municipality and population size. For water, stormwater and wastewater the tables give asset counts and lengths, physical condition ratings, year of construction, expected useful life, asset management plans and information systems, and the number of owners whose wastewater systems need upgrading to meet effluent standards. It runs every two years (reference years 2016 to 2022, the 2024 cycle collected in 2025) and tables are free to download as CSV under the Statistics Canada Open Licence. Caveats: results are aggregated survey estimates, not asset-level records, and some earlier tables are archived as inactive. Simulation uses: condition and age profiles for ageing and renewal planning, capacity planning and climate adaptation of water networks. Related record: the US Clean Watersheds Needs Survey (data-epa-clean-watersheds-needs-survey-2022).

notes: Harvested as individual StatCan tables (34-10-0211 to 34-10-0269 series) and as Dataverse copies of the 2016, 2018 and 2020 data tables; all are covered by this record. The licence is Statistics Canada's general Open Licence (page read); the example table page returned 'upstream request failed' twice, so table-level details were not read. The table titles listed in schema_summary are from the harvested candidates.
